subtitle: Lesson 21 · Data Architecture Across Hybrid and Multi-Cloud

steps.label: Egress cost
steps.sub: every cloud charges per-GB to move data out toward another cloud

steps.label: Transfer time
steps.sub: terabytes take hours, petabytes take days, even on a fast link

steps.label: Operational inertia
steps.sub: pipelines, access controls, and backups are already built around the data's location

code:
# why compute moves to data, not the reverse
compute job:      redeploy in minutes, low cost
large dataset:    egress fees + hours/days to move
                  + every downstream pipeline re-validated

result: cheapest path = run the workload
        next to the data, in whichever cloud
        the data already lives in
caption: The economical direction is almost always compute toward data, not data toward compute.

code:
stated strategy:  standardize compute on Azure
reality:          40 TB dataset has lived in AWS S3 for years
outcome:          new analytics workload runs in AWS anyway

lesson: ask "where will this data's gravity be
        in two years?" at the moment it first lands --
        not after a workload is already fighting it
caption: Data gravity frequently decides the real architecture more than the stated cloud preference does.

subtitle: How replication actually works once gravity says some data has to cross anyway.
